properties.name: loop_status answers in under 1,000 ms on the path a working session actually takes — after a write (an OBJECTIVE, not a threshold)
properties.statement:
loop_status should answer in about 1,000 ms WHEN A WRITE PRECEDES IT — the state a working session is almost always in, and the one the existing warm budget does not measure.

⭐ AN OBJECTIVE, NOT A THRESHOLD — Anthony's clarification, 2026-09-12, correcting the first draft of this node: "the under-1s was an objective, not a threshold." Missing it is not a breach and must not be reported as one; it is the direction the work points. reflow2's Constraint type carries an `objective` field only on a `kpp`, so for a `budget` this sentence is where the distinction lives — a budget_report `exceeded` against this limit means "not yet at the objective", nothing stronger.

WHY A SECOND BUDGET RATHER THAN A REVISION. `con:loop-status-warm-latency-ms` limits the WARM case (no write since the last call) to 2,000 ms and is currently MET: 1,291 ms measured 2026-09-12. But `fact:loop-status-cost-is-amplifiers-not-baseline-and-80pc-of-calls-are-automation` shows the warm case is not the case anyone waits on — the same call is 4,096 ms steady once a write precedes each one, because the derived-scan memo is keyed per write generation and a session that is WORKING invalidates it every time. A budget that only measures the state a session is rarely in cannot fail when the thing gets slow.

THE NUMBER, and the tighter derivation kept so it can be argued rather than rediscovered. Anthony set 1,000 ms as the objective across the tool surface. A STRICTER DERIVATION GIVES 332 ms: loop_nudge fires this check on PostToolUse of every reflow2 call, so it is an INSTRUMENT ATTACHED TO OTHER WORK, and an instrument should not cost more than about twice the work it observes. The median reflow2 write is 166 ms (n=76 over the 2026-09-12 ledger; 154 ms over all 115 non-loop_status calls), so 2x the work it follows is 332 ms. 1,000 ms is 6x the median write it trails.

MEASURED BEFORE THIS WAS WRITTEN, 2026-09-12, reflow2-mcp 0.59.0 release, physical copy of the live store (4,343 nodes / 25,004 edges), shared transport with --export-to, load 0.1-0.4, medians of 4:
  no write before the call   1,291 ms
  one write before each call 4,096 ms   <- this budget's quantity, 4.1x from the objective
Production median that day was 12,089 ms, because concurrency (x1.6 at four clients) and machine load (up to x6 under a cargo build) stack on top.

WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER: one machine (4 cores), release build, this store at this size, an uncontended box. Nothing about cold start, the other rollups, or a design ten times this size. And it is NOT a claim that 1,000 ms is reachable — the warm baseline alone is 1,284 ms, so reaching the objective requires the intrinsic scan cost left unstarted on 2026-09-05, not only the write tax.
